The '''2017–18 USC Trojans men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Southern California]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Led by fifth-year head coach [[Andy Enfield]], they played their home games at the [[Galen Center]] in [[Los Angeles|Los Angeles, California]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. They finished the season 24–12, 12–6 in [[2017-18 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to finish in second place. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2018 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]], they defeated [[2017-18 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|Oregon State]] in the quarterfinals and [[2017-18 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] in the semifinals before losing to [[2017-18 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] in the championship game. They were one of the last four teams not selected for the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and as a result earned a No. 1 seed in the [[2018 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]], where they defeated [[2017-18 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]] in the first round before losing to [[2017-18 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]] in the second round.

==Previous season==
The [[2016–17 USC Trojans men's basketball team|Trojans]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 26–10, 10–8 in [[2016–17 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to finish in a tie for fifth place; their 26 victories set a program record. They defeated [[2016–17 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] in the first round of the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] before losing in the quarterfinals to [[2016–17 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2016–17 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] in the First Four and [[2016–17 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]] in the First Round before losing in the Second Round to [[2016–17 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]].

==FBI investigation==
{{main|2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal}}
On September 26, federal prosecutors in New York announced charges of [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal|fraud and corruption against 10 people involved in college basketball]], including USC assistant coach Tony Bland.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/20824193/ncaa-basketball-coaches-10-charged-fraud-corruption|title=NCAA coaches among 10 arrested for corruption|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-09-26}}</ref> The charges allege that Bland and others allegedly received benefits from financial advisers and others to influence student-athletes to retain their services.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/09/26/college-basketball-assistants-arrested-fbi-fraud-corruption-scheme/703295001/|title=FBI arrests four college basketball assistants on charges of fraud|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en}}</ref> Following the announcement, USC placed Bland on administrative leave and announced that it would conduct an internal investigation of the matter.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/09/26/usc-hires-former-fbi-director-freeh-tony-bland-placed-on-leave/|title=USC hires former FBI director Freeh, Tony Bland placed on leave|date=2017-09-26|work=CollegeBasketballTalk|access-date=2017-09-26|language=en-US}}</ref> Potential [[2018 NBA draft]] pick [[De'Anthony Melton]] would be indefinitely suspended in relation to the scandal in January before leaving USC on February 21, 2018.
